`CreatedAt` / `UpdatedAt`, `db()`, RLS

### `Base`


Base class for all SQLAlchemy models.

### `CreatedAt`

```python
CreatedAt = Annotated[datetime.datetime, <sqlalchemy.orm.properties.MappedColumn object>]
```

*(no docstring)*

### `db`

```python
def db() -> AsyncSession
```

The session of the innermost open unit of the current task (§4.3):

```python
item = Item(title=body.title)
db().add(item)
await db().flush()   # never commit(): the unit owns the transaction
```

Outside any unit it raises `UnitOfWorkRequiredError` (SANDLOOM-R002); in a
request the first call opens the lazy request unit, committed when the
handler succeeds and rolled back on an exception. A child task opens its
own unit with `open_uow` (SANDLOOM-R013 otherwise).

### `new_id`

```python
def new_id() -> uuid.UUID
```

A new time-ordered id (UUIDv7, RFC 9562) for a primary key:

```python
id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(primary_key=True, default=new_id)
```

Ids sort in creation order: by time across processes, and strictly
increasing within one process (a counter orders a millisecond's burst).
So `order_by(Model.id)` is the creation order, with no tie.

### `TenantScoped`

```python
class TenantScoped
```

Mixin marking a model as tenant-owned (adds the indexed `tenant_id`).

Inheriting this both declares the column and opts the model into automatic
tenant filtering. Declare models as `class Foo(TenantScoped, Base)`.

## Advanced names

### `disable_tenant_rls`

```python
def disable_tenant_rls(op: _Executes, table: str, *, schema: str | None = None) -> None
```

Drop the Sandloom tenant policies and disable RLS on
`table` (for downgrade).

### `enable_tenant_rls`

```python
def enable_tenant_rls(
    op: _Executes,
    table: str,
    *,
    column: str = 'tenant_id',
    schema: str | None = None,
    system_access: bool = False,
    system_role: str = 'sandloom_system',
) -> None
```

Enable + FORCE PostgreSQL RLS with the Sandloom tenant policy on `table`.

`op` is the Alembic `op` module (or any object with `execute(str)`).
`column` must be the table's `uuid` tenant column (`TenantScoped`
declares `tenant_id`). `system_access=True` lets the system-channel
role (`system_role`, default `sandloom_system`; it must already exist) read
and write every tenant's rows of THIS table. Re-running is safe (policies
are replaced).

### `get_planned_reads`

```python
def get_planned_reads(request: Request) -> AsyncGenerator[Any, None]
```

The handle of a route DECLARED read-only (execution planner).

The whole handler runs inside a read-only scope: `publish_event` /
`record_audit` / `on_commit` raise. Declared operations run through
`reads.one(op, **key)` on the planner's general or optimized executor.

### `get_read_only_db`

```python
def get_read_only_db(request: Request) -> AsyncGenerator[AsyncSession, None]
```

PROTOTYPE: request session for a route DECLARED read-only.

With `DB_READ_ONLY_SESSIONS=true` statements run in a server-enforced
READ ONLY transaction. The client policy also refuses writes, flushes,
locking reads and raw statements before sending them. PostgreSQL remains
the backstop for SELECT functions with side effects. Off (default):
exactly `get_db`.

### `get_snapshot_reads`

```python
def get_snapshot_reads(request: Request) -> AsyncGenerator[Any, None]
```

`PlannedReads` with ONE snapshot: `REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY`.

Every declared read of the route runs in the route's read unit, in one
`REPEATABLE READ` read-only transaction (the default `PlannedReads` is
READ COMMITTED: two reads may see different snapshots). Use it when the
route's reads must be mutually consistent.

### `get_uow_reads`

```python
async def get_uow_reads(request: Request, db: DbSession) -> Any
```

Planned reads INSIDE the request Unit of Work (mixed routes).

Depends on `DbSession` (the SAME session the route gets: FastAPI caches
the dependency per request), so declared operations run on the UoW's
connection and transaction with the general executor: one connection,
one tenant GUC, read-your-own-writes, and the UoW's outbox / audit /
on_commit semantics unchanged (no read-only scope is opened).

### `JoinRead`

```python
class JoinRead(ReadOperation)(
    entity: type,
    result: type[R],
    by: tuple[str, ...] = ('id',),
    tenant_scoped: bool | None = None,
    database: str = 'default',
    name: str = '',
    lock: str | None = None,
    join: type | None = None,
    via: str = '',
    join_by: Mapping[str, str] = <factory>,
    join_where: Mapping[str, Any] = <factory>,
    joined_fields: Mapping[str, str] = <factory>,
) -> None
```

A declared single-row read of `entity` joined to `join` on a FK.

`entity` JOIN `join` ON `entity.<via>` = `join`'s primary key, with

* `by` — equality key columns of `entity` (call arguments); they must
  cover `entity`'s primary key or a unique constraint, so the read
  returns at most one row on EVERY executor. `via` counts towards that
  key when the join side is pinned to at most one row (`join_by` +
  `join_where` cover a unique key of `join`): a read keyed only on the
  joined row (`by=()`) is allowed when `via` is itself unique on
  `entity` (e.g. a one-to-one detail row of a customer found by its
  unique tenant id);
* `join_by` — `{argument: column of join}`: more equality arguments;
* `join_where` — `{column of join: constant}`: fixed equality filters
  (e.g. `{"is_active": True}`), sent as parameters;
* `joined_fields` — `{DTO field: attribute of join}`; every other DTO
  field is read from `entity`.

`via` must be a column of `entity` with a declared `ForeignKey` to
`join` (no guessed join conditions). Tenant scoping is inferred PER
SIDE: every `TenantScoped` table of the join gets the tenant predicate
(and RLS). Both entities must belong to the declaring module (the import
boundary rules already forbid reaching another module's models).

### `ListOperation`

```python
class ListOperation(ReadOperation)(
    entity: type,
    result: type[R],
    by: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    tenant_scoped: bool | None = None,
    database: str = 'default',
    name: str = '',
    lock: str | None = None,
    where: Mapping[str, Any] = <factory>,
    order_by: tuple[str, ...] = ('id',),
    descending: bool = False,
    max_limit: int | None = None,
    require_index: bool = True,
    join: type | None = None,
    via: str = '',
    join_by: Mapping[str, str] = <factory>,
    join_where: Mapping[str, Any] = <factory>,
    joined_fields: Mapping[str, str] = <factory>,
    optional: Mapping[str, str] = <factory>,
    prefix: Mapping[str, str] = <factory>,
    prefix_ignore_case: bool = False,
) -> None
```

A declared list read: `entity` rows, one keyset page per call.

* `by` — equality filter columns of `entity` (call arguments; may be
  empty for a tenant-scoped "all rows of my tenant" list);
* `where` — `{column of entity: constant}` fixed filters;
* `order_by` — columns of `entity`, each part of an index of its table;
  the primary key is appended as the tie-breaker (a total order, so keyset
  pages never skip or repeat a row); `descending` flips the whole order;
* `max_limit` — the declaration's page cap (never above
  `PLANNER_LIST_MAX_LIMIT`); every call passes `limit` (mandatory);
* optional `join` on a DECLARED foreign key, in either direction:
  `via` on `entity` -> `join`'s primary key (many-to-one), or `via`
  on `join` -> `entity`'s primary key (one-to-many: `via` +
  `join_by` + `join_where` must cover a unique key of `join`, so the
  join never multiplies rows); `join_by` / `join_where` /
  `joined_fields` as for `JoinRead`;
* `optional` — `{argument: column of entity}` equality filters applied
  only when the call's argument is not `None` (`None` = no filter,
  never `IS NULL`);
* `prefix` — `{argument: String column of entity}`: `column LIKE
  &lt;argument> || '%'` with the argument matched as a LITERAL prefix (its
  `%` / `_` / `\` are escaped), applied only when the argument is
  not `None`; `prefix_ignore_case=True` matches case-insensitively
  (`ILIKE`).

Optional and prefix filters are residual predicates: the covering-index
rule is about `by` + `where` (+ tenant) and the order only — a page
walks that index in order and skips non-matching rows, it never sorts.
Each combination of present filters is its own statement (at most
`MAX_OPTIONAL_FILTERS` optional + prefix filters per operation).

Pages are addressed by an opaque, tamper-evident cursor (HMAC-SHA256 over
the operation, the filter arguments, the bound tenant and the position):
the client cannot move it to another filter, tenant or position. The
tenant is never read from it. Tenant scoping is inferred per side.

#### `ListOperation.n_required`

```python
n_required  (property)
```

The number of leading `keys` that are always applied.

#### `ListOperation.page_cap`

```python
def page_cap(self) -> int
```

The effective page cap: the declaration's, never above the framework's.

### `make_cursor`

```python
def make_cursor(op: ListOperation[Any], position: Sequence[Any], /, **key: Any) -> str
```

A cursor starting after `position` (the operation's order values, in
`order_by` + primary-key order) for these filter arguments and the bound
tenant (e.g. to resume a list at a known row).

### `make_db_dependency`

```python
def make_db_dependency(
    name: str,
) -> Callable[[Request], AsyncGenerator[AsyncSession, None]]
```

Build a request dependency yielding a session for a NAMED database.

Use this when a module's endpoints must read/write a non-default database
(e.g. `"analytics"`). The module references only the logical name; the
concrete engine/driver is resolved by the infrastructure registry. Events
published while this session is the active UoW go to that database's
transactional outbox.

`DbSession` remains the canonical dependency for the default database.

### `open_uow`

```python
def open_uow(database: str | None = None) -> AbstractAsyncContextManager[AsyncSession]
```

Open a unit of work on `database` (today `db_session`, §4.3):

```python
async with open_uow() as session:
    session.add(row)          # committed when the block exits
```

One transaction, committed on success and rolled back on an exception,
with the transactional outbox for the events it publishes.

### `ReadOperation`

```python
class ReadOperation(Generic)(
    entity: type,
    result: type[R],
    by: tuple[str, ...] = ('id',),
    tenant_scoped: bool | None = None,
    database: str = 'default',
    name: str = '',
    lock: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

A declared single-row read: `entity` WHERE `by` columns = arguments.

`result` is part of the contract: the caller always gets an instance of
it (or `None`), whichever executor ran. `tenant_scoped` is inferred from
the entity; declaring it explicitly is checked against the entity (an
operation can never opt OUT of tenant scoping of a tenant-owned entity).
Identity-hashed: one object = one declared operation.

### `Reads`

```python
class Reads(
    core: CoreRuntime | None,
    unit: Any = None,
    *,
    adapter: ExecutionAdapter | None = None,
    shared: bool = False,
    contract: bool = False,
    isolation: Isolation = 'read_committed',
) -> None
```

Handle that runs declared operations.

Two modes, fixed when the handle is made:

* **read-only scope** (`unit is None`; `sandloom.core.di.PlannedReads`,
  `read_scope`): consecutive OPTIMIZED reads share a lazy read-only
  transaction per database. A GENERAL read releases that transaction and
  opens an ORM read unit; subsequent reads use that unit. Stronger isolation
  always uses one ORM transaction. A scope never holds two connections of
  one pool. A handle made without a scope
  (`shared=False`, `execute_one`) runs every operation in its own
  transaction;
* **inside a Unit of Work** (`unit` = the UoW's session;
  `sandloom.core.di.UowReads`, `sandloom.core.orm.session_reads`): every
  operation runs ON that session — the UoW's connection, transaction and
  tenant GUC — with the GENERAL executor (ORM: autoflush + identity map, so
  the read sees the unit's own writes, flushed or not). The optimized
  executor is never used there (see the design doc, "mixed operations").

#### `Reads.in_unit_of_work`

```python
in_unit_of_work  (property)
```

#### `Reads.one`

```python
async def one(self, op: ReadOperation[R], /, **key: Any) -> R | None
```

Run `op` for `key` (the hot path: one adapter lookup, no wrappers).

#### `Reads.page`

```python
async def page(
    self,
    op: ListOperation[R],
    /,
    *,
    limit: int,
    cursor: str | None = None,
    **key: Any,
) -> Page[R]
```

One keyset page of `op` for the filter arguments `key`.

`limit` is mandatory and capped (`ListOperation.page_cap`,
`PageLimitError`); `cursor` is the previous page's
`next_cursor` and is verified BEFORE any I/O (`InvalidCursor`).

#### `Reads.aclose`

```python
async def aclose(self) -> None
```

End the scope's read units (the scope owner calls it, once).

### `session_reads`

```python
def session_reads(session: Any) -> sandloom.core.planner.Reads
```

Run declared operations ON `session` (an open Unit of Work).

Inside a `DbSession` route, `db_session()` or `contract_session()`:
the reads share the unit's transaction, connection and tenant context
(read-your-own-writes; the general executor). Routes use
`sandloom.core.di.UowReads` instead.
